rot.knightMates.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: this position is from a Lichess game that began with the Englund Gambit. The black king on e8 is surrounded by its own pieces: the queen on d8, the bishops on d7 and f8, the knight on e7 and the pawn on f7.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex1.p: Find the knight move that gives mate.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex1.certo: Yes, it is mate: the knight checks on d6, and the king has no free square.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex1.revela: The knight goes to d6 and gives mate: the king is surrounded by its own pieces, and none of them can block a knight check.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex1.err.b5c7.1: The knight checks on c7, but that square is attacked by the queen on d8 and the knight on a6.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex1.err.b5c7.2: With this move Black has a resource: the knight on a6 captures yours, and the mate is gone.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex1.err.b5c7.3: Back to the position: look for a knight check on a square no black piece attacks.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not give mate. Look for the knight check: the black king has no free square.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the knight check.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex1.l1: This is the smothered mate: the king is surrounded by its own pieces, and the knight gives a check that no piece can block, because it jumps.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex1.l2: Nobody can capture the knight: the bishop on d7 blocks the queen, the knight on e7 blocks the bishop on f8, and the bishop on f4 also defends d6. In positions like this, check that the knight lands on a square no black piece attacks.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: the black king is in the corner, on a8, and its own rook on b8 occupies a square next to it. The knight on c6 watches a7 and b8.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.p: Find the rook move that gives mate.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.certo: Yes, it is mate: the rook checks on a7, and the knight on c6 defends it, so the king cannot capture it.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.revela: The rook goes to a7 and gives mate: the knight on c6 defends the rook, and the rook watches b7.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.err.c6b8.1: The knight captures the rook on b8, but without check and on a square defended by the rook on h8.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.err.c6b8.2: With this move Black has a resource: the rook on h8 recaptures, and Black still has a rook and a bishop against your rook.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.err.c6b8.3: Back to the position: look for the rook check supported by the knight.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.err.c6e5.1: The knight captures the bishop, but without check, and stops watching a7.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.err.c6e5.2: With this move Black has a resource: the rook on b8 captures the b2 pawn and threatens to go down to the first rank, where your king is trapped by its pawns.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.err.c6e5.3: Back to the position: look for the rook check supported by the knight.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not give mate. Look for a rook check on a square the knight defends.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: look for the rook check next to the king.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex2.l1: This is the Arabian mate: the rook checks right next to the king, and the knight defends the rook. Here Black's own rook on b8 occupies the last square.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.e1: Attack: the black king is on g7, and the knight on f6 watches g8 and h7. The pawn on g5 defends the knight.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.p: Find the rook move that gives mate.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.certo: Yes, it is mate: the rook checks on g8, the knight defends the rook, and the pawn on g5 defends the knight.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.revela: The rook goes to g8 and gives mate: the knight on f6 defends the rook, and the pawn on g5 defends the knight.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.err.f6e8.1: The knight checks on e8, but stops watching g8 and h7.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.err.f6e8.2: With this move Black has a resource: the king goes to f8 and gets out of check. Without the knight on f6, there is no mate any more.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.err.f6e8.3: Back to the position: look for the rook check supported by the knight.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.err.f6d5.1: The knight captures the one on d5, but without check.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.err.f6d5.2: With this move Black has a resource: the pawn on e6 recaptures, and the material is level.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.err.f6d5.3: Back to the position: look for the rook check supported by the knight.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.fora: That move does not give mate. Look for a rook check on a square the knight defends.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.volta: Try again: look for the rook check supported by the knight.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.l1: This is the hook mate: the rook gives check, the knight defends the rook, and a pawn defends the knight. The rook watches f8 and h8, and the pawn on g5 also watches h6.
rot.knightMates.ideia.ex3.l2: In positions like this, the supported knight closes the squares the rook cannot reach. In all three mates, the knight and the king's squares decide.
rot.knightMates.demos.blackburne.1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side. This position comes from a well-known opening trap, the Blackburne Shilling Gambit. The white king on e1 is surrounded by its own pieces.
rot.knightMates.demos.blackburne.2: The knight goes to f3 and gives check. The bishop on e2 cannot capture: that would leave the king in check from the queen on e4. The king has no square: it is a smothered mate.
rot.knightMates.demos.blackburne.3: In positions like this, before the smothered mate, also check the piece that seems to defend the square: it may be tied to its king.
rot.knightMates.demos.anastasia.1: Attack: back to White. The black king is on h7, on the edge file, with the pawn on g7 beside it. The knight on e7 watches g8 and g6.
rot.knightMates.demos.anastasia.p: Find the rook move that gives mate.
rot.knightMates.demos.anastasia.certo: Yes, it is mate: the rook checks along the h-file, and the knight takes away g6 and g8.
rot.knightMates.demos.anastasia.revela: The rook goes to h5 and gives mate: the check comes along the h-file, and the knight on e7 takes away g6 and g8.
rot.knightMates.demos.anastasia.err.d5d7: The rook goes to the seventh rank, but without check, and your knight on e7 blocks its way to f7.
With this move Black has a resource: the rook on a8 goes to d8 and attacks your rook, and Black is still ahead in material.
Back to the position: look for the rook check along the edge file.
rot.knightMates.demos.anastasia.2: This is Anastasia's mate: the knight closes the squares next to the king, and the rook checks along the edge file. The pawn on g7 occupies the last square.
rot.knightMates.demos.xequeAntes.1: Attack: Black again. The white king on c1 is surrounded by the rook on d1, the queen on d2 and the pawns on b2 and c2. Only the b1 square is free.
rot.knightMates.demos.xequeAntes.2: The queen goes to a1 and checks along the first rank. The king cannot go to b1, which the queen watches, and the only defence is to block the check.
rot.knightMates.demos.xequeAntes.3: The knight on c3 blocks on b1, the only move. Now it fills the king's last free square.
rot.knightMates.demos.xequeAntes.4: The knight on b4 goes to a2 and gives a smothered mate: the king is surrounded by its own pieces, and the queen on a1 defends the knight.
rot.knightMates.demos.xequeAntes.5: In positions like this, a check first forces a piece to fill the king's last free square, and the knight gives the mate.
rot.knightMates.demos.philidor.1: Attack: back to White. The black king on h8 is trapped by the pawns on g7 and h7, and only the g8 square is free. The knight on h6 watches g8 and f7, and the queen on d5 can reach g8.
rot.knightMates.demos.philidor.p: Find the check that forces Black to occupy the g8 square.
rot.knightMates.demos.philidor.certo: Yes: the queen checks on g8. See why giving up the queen works.
rot.knightMates.demos.philidor.revela: The right move is the queen check on g8: the piece that captures it will fill the king's last square.
The knight checks on f7, but that square is attacked by the rook on f8.
With this move Black has a resource: the rook on f8 captures the knight, and the mate is gone.
Back to the position: look for the check that forces a black piece onto g8.
rot.knightMates.demos.philidor.2: The king cannot capture the queen, because the knight on h6 defends g8. The only defence is for the rook on f8 to capture.
rot.knightMates.demos.philidor.3: The rook captures the queen, the only move. Now it blocks the king's last free square, and nobody defends f7 any more.
rot.knightMates.demos.philidor.4: The knight goes to f7 with a smothered mate. Giving up the queen paid off: the forced capture closed g8.
rot.knightMates.demos.philidor.5: In positions like this, a piece given up with check forces the opponent to occupy their own king's last square. Before giving it up, check that the capture is forced.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.1: Attack: back to White. The black king on g8 has its own pawns in front, the rook on h8 beside it and only f8 free. The knight on d5 can reach e7 with check, but the rook on e8 defends that square.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.p: Before the knight check, count who defends e7. Which move works?
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.certo: Yes: the rook captures the one on e8 with check and removes the defender of e7. See why the knight comes afterwards.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.revela: The right move is for the rook to capture the one on e8 with check: the black rook was the defender of e7.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.err.d5e7.1: The knight checks on e7, and it looks like a smothered mate. But the rook on e8 defends that square.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.err.d5e7.2: With this move Black has a resource: the rook on e8 captures the knight, and the mate is gone.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.err.d5e7.3: Back to the position: look for the move that removes the defender of e7 with check.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.err.d5f6.1: The knight checks on f6, but that square is attacked by the knight on d7 and the pawn on g7.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.err.d5f6.2: With this move Black has a resource: the knight on d7 captures yours, and Black wins another piece.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.err.d5f6.3: Back to the position: look for the move that removes the defender of e7 with check.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.2: The king has no square: f8 is on the line of the check. Black has to block.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.3: The knight on d7 blocks on f8, the only move. Now it fills the king's last free square.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.4: The knight goes to e7 with a smothered mate: the black rook is gone, and no black piece attacks e7. The king is surrounded by the knight on f8, the rook on h8 and the pawns.
rot.knightMates.demos.excecao.5: In positions like this, before the knight check, count who defends the square. If a piece defends it, remove the defender with a check first.
rot.knightMates.pratica.valeAqui.err.e6g: The bishop captures the rook on g8, but without check, and the black king gets that square back. Black mates first, with checks against your king.
rot.knightMates.pratica.valeAqui.enuncia: Back to White. Black threatens your king, but it is your move. The black king on h8 is almost surrounded, and your queen stands on f7. Does the smothered mate work here? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.knightMates.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The queen checked on g8, and the rook on d8 had to capture, because the bishop on e6 watches that square. With g8 filled, the knight went to f7 with a smothered mate.
rot.knightMates.pratica.valeAqui.err.f7f: With the check on f8 you give up the queen: the rook on d8 and the bishop on g7 defend that square.
rot.knightMates.pratica.valeAqui.err.f7g: The queen captures the bishop with check, but the king captures it, and Black is ahead in material.
rot.knightMates.pratica.valeAqui.err.b2c: Capturing the rook on c3 opens the b-file in front of your king, and Black attacks with checks. Look first for a check against the black king.
rot.knightMates.pratica.valeAqui.err.f7e: The queen leaves f7 without giving check, and Black mates first: the rook on c3 captures the bishop on c1 with check, the king takes it, and the queen comes in on b2.
With the check on e8 you give up the queen: the rook on d8 captures it.
rot.knightMates.pratica.englund.enunciad: Now let us think from Black's side, in a Lichess game that began with the Englund Gambit. The white king on e1 has not castled yet. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.knightMates.pratica.englund.fim: The knight checked on d3, and the white king was surrounded by its own pieces. The pawn on e2 could not capture: that would leave the king in check from the queen on e7. It was a smothered mate.
rot.knightMates.pratica.englund.err.e5f3: The knight captures the one on f3 with check, but the knight on d2 recaptures, and the game stays equal. Look for the check the white king cannot escape.
rot.knightMates.pratica.centro.enunciado: Back to White. The black king is in the centre, on e5, next to its own pawns. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.knightMates.pratica.centro.fim: The rook checked on e6, defended by the knight on f4, and the pawn on g3 defends the knight. The knight also watches d5, and the black pawns block d4 and f5: the hook mate works in the centre too.
rot.knightMates.pratica.centro.err.f4d3: The knight checks on d3, but the king escapes to e4, and the mate is gone. Look for the rook check supported by the knight.
rot.knightMates.pratica.centro.err.a4a5: The pawn advances without check, and the black d4 pawn races to promote. Look for the rook check supported by the knight.
rot.knightMates.pratica.centro.err.b4b5: The pawn advances without check, and the black d4 pawn races to promote. Look for the rook check supported by the knight.
rot.knightMates.pratica.centro.err.h6c6: The rook goes to c6 without check, and Black gains time with the d4 pawn. Look for the rook check supported by the knight.
